summary: Telegram-controlled remote shell backdoor shipped as typosquat of requests/httpx
details: The package presents itself as an HTTP client (name httpz-requests) but its actual payload is a Telegram bot that provides remote shell access on the host that imports it. Importing the package runs bot.start_bot from __init__.py, which connects to Telegram and dispatches incoming messages into an on-host execution engine (bot/handlers/core.so). Commands received from Telegram are decoded via an obfuscate module (base64 + XOR, exported symbols enc_b64 and _xor.genexpr) before being executed, and the package documentation explicitly states that commands are executed in encoded form so they do not appear as plaintext in the process list or logs. Whoever controls the Telegram bot token has full remote code execution on any machine that installs and imports this package. Publisher metadata is unfilled (author 'Aapka Naam <you@example.com>', homepage pointing at 'YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME'), and the distribution name typosquats the widely used requests / httpx libraries, so a developer who mistypes an HTTP client name pulls in a remote-shell backdoor instead.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
